definitions.explanation: lack of loyalty or faithfulness, especially toward a lord, superior, or spouse

examples.japanese: {不忠|ふちゅう}な⟦{家臣|かしん}→家臣：12655_kashin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{追放|ついほう}→追放：14313_tsuihou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。

examples.english: He was punished for the crime of disloyalty.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}→戦国時代：19200_sengokujidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{主君|しゅくん}→主君：11712_shukun⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{不忠|ふちゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{重|おも}い→重い：00804_omoi⟧⟦{罪|つみ}→罪：03532_tsumi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されていた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the Warring States period, disloyalty to one's lord was considered one of the gravest offenses.

notes:
Composed of {不|ふ} (non-; un-) + {忠|ちゅう} (loyalty; faithfulness). Historically refers to betrayal of feudal loyalty, but can also describe unfaithfulness in other relationships. Most commonly encountered in historical and literary contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不忠|ふちゅう}な⟦{家臣|かしん}→家臣：12655_kashin⟧: disloyal retainer
- {不忠|ふちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{罪|つみ}→罪：03532_tsumi⟧: the crime of disloyalty
- {不忠|ふちゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to commit an act of disloyalty
- {不忠|ふちゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{責|せ}める→責める：02284_semeru⟧: to blame someone for disloyalty

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{裏切|うらぎ}り→裏切り：17967_uragiri⟧: betrayal; treachery — more emotionally charged and broader in usage
- ⟦{忠義|ちゅうぎ}→忠義：20670_chuugi⟧: loyalty; devotion — the positive counterpart to {不忠|ふちゅう}
- {不貞|ふてい}: infidelity; adultery — specifically refers to marital unfaithfulness
